deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a set of successive, heavily corrected drafts of the opening of Riemann's speculative natural-philosophical and psychological theory of 'Geistesmasse' (mind-mass). It sits between a page of wave-optics work, where ω' and ω'' are the forward and backward travelling waves and ω_tt = c^2 ω_ξξ, and a private family letter.

The content, in order:

(a) A heading, roughly 'Hypothesen über Erinnerung u. Einbildungskraft' (hypotheses on memory and imagination).

(b) First draft. With every mental act something lasting enters our soul. It does not exert a lasting influence on the phenomena; it shows itself as such only under special circumstances.

(c) The physical counterpart. Into every ponderable atom, at every instant, enters a definite quantity of matter proportional to the gravitational force, and there it disappears, without lasting effect on the phenomena. Reformulated: in every ponderable atom, matter passes continually from the corporeal world into the mental world. There is an unfinished line, 'Die Bewegungsform des verschwindenden Stoffes' (the form of motion of the disappearing matter).

(d) Several restatements of the basic hypothesis. In every act of our mental life something lasting is formed (Riemann replaced 'erzeugt' by 'gebildet'). This lasting thing he calls 'Geistesmasse'. Each representation (Vorstellung) is thus the formation of a new mind-mass entering the soul, and equal representations correspond to equally formed mind-masses.

(e) Newly formed mind-masses combine in a definite way and to a definite degree with older ones. The soul is a compact mind-mass, connected in the most intimate and manifold ways. It grows continually through newly entering mind-masses, and its development (Fortbildung) rests on this.

(f) Right column: a critique of the hypothesis of the soul as a unitary bearer of what is lasting.
- That hypothesis rests, first, on the connectedness and mutual conditioning of all representations.
- But a unitary bearer does not suffice to explain the specific connections between particular representations. Their cause must be sought in the representations themselves.
- Once that cause is admitted, a unitary bearer of all representations is 'überflüssig' (superfluous). The final word is probably 'falsch' (false), but the reading is uncertain.

The problem being served is a field-theoretic, ether-type unification of gravitation, light and mind. The gravitational 'sink' of matter in ponderable atoms is matched by the formation of mind-masses. This is the programme published posthumously in Riemann's Werke (1876; Weber–Dedekind) as 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' and 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'.
errors: No mathematical steps exist, so nothing can be checked for correctness.

The physical hypothesis has matter continually flowing into ponderable atoms at a rate proportional to the gravitational force, then disappearing. It is a speculative sink model of gravitation and is not accepted physics, though it is internally coherent as a hypothesis.
The philosophical argument in (f) reaches its conclusion ('superfluous') only by assertion. It is not demonstrated, and the drafts break off.

The sentence 'Die Bildung gleichgeformter Geistesmassen ist also ist nur gleicher Vorstellungen bei' is grammatically broken. It is an abandoned draft, rewritten immediately below as 'Bei gleichen Vorstellungen werden gleich geformte Geistesmassen gebildet'.

results.what: Hypothesis that every mental act forms a lasting 'Geistesmasse'; the soul is a compact, manifoldly connected mind-mass growing by accretion
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann himself, posthumous publication in Werke 1876 ('Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'); influenced by J.F. Herbart

results.what: Matter enters every ponderable atom at a rate proportional to gravitational force and disappears there (passing into the mental world)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (Werke 1876); similar ether-sink ideas later in Bjerknes, Yarkovsky and others

results.what: Critique of the soul as unitary substrate: connections between representations must be explained by the representations themselves
results.usually_credited_to: Hume / Herbart tradition; Riemann's version is published in his philosophical fragments

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds working drafts of passages already published in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'. These include the Geistesmasse concept, the soul as a 'compacte aufs Innigste u. Mannigfachste verbundene Geistesmasse', and gravitation-proportional matter disappearing into atoms. They are well known as his, and the page contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 'In jedes ponderabeln Atoms tritt' should read 'In jedes ponderable Atom tritt'. The image shows no genitive -s, matching the published wording 'In jedes ponderable Atom tritt in jedem Augenblick eine bestimmte, der Gravitationskraft proportionale Stoffmenge ein und verschwindet dort'.
The heading likely reads 'Hypothesen über Erinnerung u. Einbildungskraft' ('ü.' abbreviation); '[?]' can be resolved tentatively.

Second line of the page: the reading 'in Folge des Seelenlebens beständig' is doubtful. The image suggests an interlinear insertion more like 'in Folge jedes ... beständig' and should remain marked uncertain.

The broken right-column sentence 'Die Bildung gleichgeformter Geistesmassen ist also / ist nur gleicher Vorstellungen bei / Vorstellungen werden gleich geformte Geistesmassen gebildet' is best read as a correction sequence whose surviving text is 'Bei gleichen Vorstellungen werden gleich geformte Geistesmassen gebildet'.
In the final right-column line the last word after 'überflüssig u.' is uncertain; 'falsch' is plausible but not secure.
'(ohne einen dauernden Einwirkung' should be 'ohne eine dauernde Einwirkung' or similar; the case endings in the machine transcription are unreliable here.
